O my aid in my distress, and O my companion in my hardship, and O my guardian in my prosperity, and O my helper in my desire.

He (peace be upon him) said: And it was from the supplication of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): 'O Allah, You wrote the traces, and You knew the news, and You inspected the secrets, so You settled between us and the hearts; therefore the secret with You is open, and the hearts are directed to You, and Your command for a thing when You intend it is that You say to it: Be, so it becomes.'

So say with Your mercy to Your obedience that it should enter into every limb of my limbs, and do not leave me until I meet You; and say with Your mercy to Your disobedience that it should exit from every limb of my limbs, so it does not approach me until I meet You; and provide me from the world, and make me ascetic in it, and do not turn it away from me while I have desire for it, O the Beneficent.

key_terms.غِيَاثِي: My helper or one who gives aid

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for placing obedience in the limbs and removing disobedience?
ai.summary: This supplication, attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and citing the prayer of Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), emphasizes divine omniscience and the ease of creation ('Con, so it is') to seek internal transformation. It requests that obedience permeate every limb while disobedience departs, balancing detachment from worldly allure with a healthy desire for it, reflecting the Shia concept of *zuhd* without asceticism.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Yaoub Bin Shuayb,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘O my<sup>asws</sup> Aider during my<sup>asws</sup> complains, and my<sup>asws</sup> Companions during my<sup>asws</sup> difficulties, and O my<sup>asws</sup> Guardian in my<sup>asws</sup> Bounties, and O my<sup>asws</sup> Helper during my<sup>asws</sup> wishes!’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And it was from the supplications of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘(Say), ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Write down the impacts, and Know the information, and are Notified upon the secrets. You<sup>azwj</sup> are Situated between us and the hearts, therefore the secret with You<sup>azwj</sup> is open, and the hearts are broken up to You<sup>azwj</sup>, and rather Your<sup>azwj</sup> Command for something when You<sup>azwj</sup> Intend it is that You<sup>azwj</sup> are Saying to it: “Be”, so it comes into being.

So, Say with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy to Your<sup>azwj</sup> obedience to enter into every part of my body parts, and not to separate from me until I meet You<sup>azwj</sup>. And Say with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy to Your<sup>azwj</sup> disobedience that it should exit from every part of my body parts, so it would not come near me until I meet You<sup>azwj</sup>; and Grace me from the world, and Cause me to be ascetic therein, and not to impede me and my wishes therein, O Beneficent!’’.
en.sarwar: 30. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “Say, ‘O my asset in my pain and suffering, O my companion in my severe hardships, O my benefactor, and O my abundant rain fall whenever I may desire.’ “The Imam said that of the supplications of Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) is the following: ‘O Lord, You have written down the consequences, know the news, have information about the secrets, You have taken over the place between us and (our) hearts, thus, secrets are public to You and the hearts have over flown (with desire to come to you). Your command upon a thing, whenever You will, is only Your saying, ‘Be,’ it then comes into existence,
say through Your kindness to Your obedience to enter in all and every part of my parts and do not depart from me until I will meet You,

and say through Your kindness to disobedience to You to move out of all and every part of my parts and do not ever approach me thereafter until I will meet You, provide me sustenance in this world but make me live with a reduced amount and do not isolate me whenever I desire it, (sustenance) O the Beneficent one.’”
